newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thais ban E.Timor activists before Clinton visit.
newsitem.headline: Thais ban E.Timor activists before Clinton visit.

text.p: Thailand has banned 45 East Timor activists from entering the country ahead of the visit of U.S. President Bill Clinton on November 25-26, Thai police said on Saturday.
The ban, which would be in effect from now until after Clinton departs, was aimed at preventing any embarrassing disturbances from taking place during the visit, a police spokesman told Reuters.
"We have the names of these people and cannot allow them in to cause problems during the President's visit," he said.
The activists from various Asian nations were known to operate in groups in the region and had been identified by the police, the spokesman said.

Malaysian police last weekend detained and subsequently released more than 100 East Timor activists, journalists and others who participated in the Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor II in Kuala Lumpur.
The 46 foreign participants attending the meeting were deported by the authorities.
The meeting was broken up by youths allied to the Malaysian government, who smashed into the meeting at a hotel in Kuala Lumpur, overturning furniture and manhandling participants.
The conference was held to mark the anniversary of the 1991 killing by Indonesian troops of at least 50 demonstrators in East Timor's capital of Dili.
The Malaysian government had objected to the conference saying it could harm ties with neighbouring Indonesia.

Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it the next year, a move never recognised by the United Nations, which regards Lisbon as the territory's administering power.
